glossary.Protrudes: Pushes out beyond its normal position.
glossary.Diaphragm: The dome-shaped muscle separating the chest from the abdomen.
glossary.Heartburn: A burning feeling behind the breastbone caused by acid reflux.
glossary.Regurgitation: Stomach contents coming back up into the mouth without vomiting.
glossary.Belching: Bringing up wind from the stomach through the mouth.
glossary.Insidious: Coming on gradually and subtly, so it is hard to say when it began.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.Necrosis: Death of tissue, often from loss of blood supply.
glossary.Obstruction: A blockage stopping contents passing through the gut.
glossary.Volvulus: Twisting of part of the gut around itself, which can cut off its blood supply.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, meaning the blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.Endoscopy: Looking inside the gut with a flexible camera tube.
glossary.Red flags: Symptoms suggesting serious disease such as cancer, needing urgent investigation.
glossary.Stomach bubble: Gas in the stomach, seen as a dark rounded area on X-ray.
glossary.Fundoplication: Surgery wrapping the top of the stomach around the lower oesophagus to stop reflux.
glossary.Hernia reduction: Pushing herniated tissue back to its normal position.
glossary.Herniation: Protrusion of an organ through an opening in the wall that normally contains it.
glossary.Erosions: Shallow breaks in the lining that do not go as deep as an ulcer.
glossary.Anti-reflux barrier: The LOS and diaphragm together, which normally stop acid flowing back up.
glossary.Chronic cough: A cough lasting more than 8 weeks; it raises pressure in the abdomen.
glossary.Diaphragmatic hiatus: The opening in the diaphragm through which the oesophagus passes.
glossary.Pinch point: Where the diaphragm squeezes the herniated stomach, causing friction and erosions.
glossary.Gastric fundus: The dome-shaped upper part of the stomach, above the oesophageal entry.
glossary.Acid reflux: Backward flow of stomach acid into the oesophagus.
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle in the walls of the gut, including the LOS.
